copy-030: Choose what comes along. The app prepares MP3 files and transfers them to your selected Shokz volume.
copy-032: Search YouTube Music. Pick a few tracks or an entire playlist, then follow their progress in a single queue.
copy-034: One book. One folder. One MP3.
copy-035: Browse your Audiobookshelf server and choose your books. Tracks are merged in the order supplied by the server.
copy-038: Check available space, create folders and import local MP3 files. Name conflicts keep both files under different names.
copy-040: 02 / For stories that go the distance
copy-041:
Keep the thread.
To the very last chapter.
copy-042: One MP3 per book prevents the headset from reordering its separate files. The content follows the Audiobookshelf track order, even when filenames are not alphabetical.
copy-043: Before the book, an optional local male voice can announce its title and author. Default speed: 95%. Then 3 seconds of silence, and the story begins.
copy-048: Piper and its voices are bundled. Speech synthesis works offline.
copy-049: Set up my first book ↗
attr-051: Audiobookshelf tab with a fictional server, a library and four books, one selected
copy-055: The app buttons are in English. This guide uses their exact names so you can find them easily.
copy-058: Connect the headset by USB and open its storage on your computer.
copy-059: In Shokz device / files, choose the detected device. If needed, use Select device folder to select its mounted volume.
copy-060: Check its name and available space. For music, create or choose a destination folder.
copy-061: Wait for transfers to finish, then eject the device from your operating system before unplugging it.
copy-062: Import MP3 files already on my computer
copy-063: Open your chosen folder in the device tab, click Add local MP3 and select your files. The app copies them without re-encoding: their quality and metadata stay as they are. Use New folder to create a folder and Move selected… to organise files already on the headset.
attr-065: Shokz file browser with the selected volume, free space and several music and audiobook folders
copy-066: The selected storage remains visible in the device tab.
copy-069: In YouTube Music, enter a query and choose Songs or Playlists, then Search.
copy-070: Select tracks using Ctrl or Shift, then Download / transfer selected. Choose a folder if prompted.
copy-071: For a playlist, double-click to open it and use Download whole playlist. Its folder is created automatically.
copy-072: Follow the steps in the queue. Something failed? Select its row and use Retry selected.
copy-074: Click Connect YouTube Music and follow the dialog to import headers from a /browse request in your music.youtube.com session. Then use My playlists. Public search works without signing in.
attr-076: Fictional music tracks and a queue showing a completed transfer, a conversion and a waiting track
copy-077: Several downloads can run at once; writes to the headset are coordinated.
copy-079: Choose the stories to take along.
copy-081: In Audiobookshelf, enter Server (the full URL), Username and Password, then click Connect.
copy-082: Choose your library, search for a title or author, and select books to transfer using <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> or <kbd>Shift</kbd>.
copy-083: Click Download / transfer selected books. A dialog opens for each book: keep or disable the spoken introduction, then choose Queue book. Skip book leaves that book out.
copy-084: The app downloads, converts, merges and copies the book into its own folder. Wait for the complete status.
copy-085: Your Audiobookshelf account needs download permission. The password is saved only if you tick the corresponding option.
attr-087: Export dialog with the title and author announcement enabled, the spoken text, a three-second pause and Queue book and Skip book buttons
copy-088: Each book keeps its own export choices.
copy-090: An introduction in your own words.
copy-091: Open Settings and choose the male voice Tom for French or John for English.
copy-092: Keep the 95% speed or adjust it between 60 and 120%.
copy-093: Customise the text with $book_name and $author_name. The preview shows the result; $$ inserts a dollar sign.
copy-094: Click Save settings. These choices apply to books added to the queue afterwards.
attr-097: Real Piper speech settings with the male French voice Tom, 95% speed and a template preview
copy-098: The voice volume is normalised before the silence is added.
copy-101: Choose your operating system’s executable in the GitHub releases. Portable builds include their dependencies.
copy-105: Download Shokz-Refill-linux-x86_64, make it executable and launch it.
copy-108: Feature availability. The screenshots and guide show the current application. The older 2026.41.1 release predates Audiobookshelf, book merging and Piper. Use a newer release for these features and check its release notes.
copy-112: The app targets Shokz headsets with USB MP3 storage, including OpenSwim Pro. If a volume’s name is not recognised, select its folder manually. Playback behaviour depends on the model and firmware.
copy-113: Do chapters stay in the right order?
copy-114: For Audiobookshelf exports, tracks are merged in the order supplied by the server. The headset therefore cannot reorder chapters within this single MP3. The app does not guarantee the playback order of separate tracks or books.
copy-115: What if I transfer the same content twice?
copy-116: Recognised identical exports are skipped. Unidentified files and name conflicts are preserved. A new version of a book, for example with a different introduction, gets a new numbered folder.
copy-117: How do I resume after a disconnection?
copy-118: Reconnect and select the same device. Use Retry selected for a queue item, or Resume interrupted copies for interrupted copies. The app validates partial files before resuming and checks integrity before finalising the file.
copy-119: Does the voice need Internet access?
copy-120: No. Piper and the voice models are included in current portable builds. The announcement is generated locally. Downloading media requires access to YouTube Music or your Audiobookshelf server.
copy-121: Is there a limit for long books?
copy-122: Exports that would exceed the conservative 4 GiB per-file MP3 limit are refused. Allow space on your computer for source and intermediate files too.
